verdict: OK to lend in Sri City electrical equipment, pumps and motors — back established component and pump makers selling into AP's grid and motor demand, structure tightly around working capital, and decline thin-margin assemblers with no order book.
title: Sri City Electrical Equipment, Pumps & Motors: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**These units wind copper, stamp laminations, cast housings and assemble pumps, motors and switchgear, then sell into power utilities, irrigation, construction and OEM supply chains.** Cash comes in on dispatch, but the money is made or lost in copper and steel buying, labour hours per unit and how long receivables sit with utility and OEM buyers. **Value sits in design, testing and after-sales service, not in assembly; pricing power is thin because buyers tender on price.** So when a proposal lands, check the share of revenue from repeat OEM or utility orders versus one-off tenders; if it is mostly one-off tenders, ask for the last three years' order pipeline and win rate.

## What has changed now
**The demand signal is strong: AP electricity demand is up 18.1% Apr-to-date against India's 9.5%, and NIC 27 output is up 30.9% YoY nationally [D].** Exports of the wider engineering basket are up 19.8% Apr-to-date in USD [D]. **So when a proposal lands, check whether growth is coming with falling margins; if PAT is falling while revenue rises, ask for the raw-material pass-through clause and the customer-wise price revision history.**

## Where the growth is
**Pursue tier-2 component makers and pump assemblers with a named utility or OEM customer, and units adding a testing or service line that lifts realisations.** The AP demand number [D] supports irrigation pumps and distribution equipment; the export number [D] supports exporters with dollar receivables. **If the borrower is a Japanese subsidiary in the park, ask for the parent guarantee; if the parent will not guarantee, treat it as a standalone SME.**
**If the borrower asks for a term loan for a new line, ask for the confirmed order that justifies it; if there is none, decline the term loan and keep the limit working-capital only.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch debtor days stretching, inventory of finished pumps building, and power-cost or wage lines rising faster than sales.** Shakti's margin contraction [5][7] is the template.
